The Understanding Elementary Shapes chapter is a dependable source of marks in the CTET Paper II (Classes VI–VIII) Mathematics section. This guide explains what CTET Understanding Elementary Shapes actually tests, the facts worth memorising, the mistakes that quietly cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now to see where you stand.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CTET Paper 2 asks on Understanding Elementary Shapes

Questions cover types of angles, classification of triangles and quadrilaterals, and the faces, edges and vertices of 3-D solids, including angle-sum properties.

Key facts & formulas to remember

  • Acute < 90°, right = 90°, obtuse is between 90° and 180°, straight = 180°, reflex is between 180° and 360°.
  • Angle sum of a triangle = 180°; of a quadrilateral = 360°.
  • Triangles by sides: equilateral, isosceles, scalene; by angles: acute, right, obtuse.
  • A cube/cuboid has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.
  • Euler’s formula for solids: F + V − E = 2.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Mislabelling a reflex angle as obtuse.
  • Forgetting the triangle angle sum is exactly 180°.
  • Miscounting faces, edges or vertices of a solid.

quiz.title: CTET Understanding Elementary Shapes Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten CTET Paper II–pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: CTET Paper 2 Maths: Understanding Elementary Shapes

questions.q: An angle whose measure is greater than that of a right angle and less than a straight angle is called a:
questions.explanation: An angle greater than 90 degrees (right angle) and less than 180 degrees (straight angle) is defined as an obtuse angle.

questions.q: If the measure of an angle is 35 degrees, then the measure of its complementary angle is:
questions.explanation: Two angles are complementary if their sum is 90 degrees. Therefore, the complement of 35 degrees = 90 degrees - 35 degrees = 55 degrees.

questions.q: Two supplementary angles are in the ratio 2 : 3. What is the measure of the smaller angle?
questions.explanation: Let the angles be 2x and 3x. Since they are supplementary, 2x + 3x = 180 degrees, so 5x = 180 degrees and x = 36 degrees. The smaller angle is 2x = 2 x 36 degrees = 72 degrees.

questions.q: A triangle having sides of lengths 7 cm, 7 cm, and 10 cm is classified as:
questions.explanation: A triangle with two equal sides (7 cm and 7 cm) and one different side is called an isosceles triangle.

questions.q: Which of the following quadrilaterals has diagonals that are always equal in length and bisect each other at right angles?
questions.explanation: A square is a quadrilateral whose diagonals are equal in length and perpendicular bisectors of each other.

questions.q: The longest chord of a circle is always its:
questions.explanation: A diameter is a chord that passes through the center of the circle and is the longest possible chord in any circle.

questions.q: How many faces, vertices, and edges does a rectangular prism (cuboid) have respectively?
questions.explanation: A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces, 8 vertices, and 12 edges.

questions.q: The interior angles of a triangle are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. What is the measure of the largest angle?
questions.explanation: Let the angles be x, 2x, and 3x. Sum of angles in a triangle = 180 degrees, so x + 2x + 3x = 180 degrees, 6x = 180 degrees, x = 30 degrees. The largest angle is 3x = 3 x 30 degrees = 90 degrees.

questions.q: In a triangle PQR, side QR is produced to point S. If angle PRS = 110 degrees and angle PQR = 45 degrees, what is the measure of angle QPR?
questions.explanation: By the exterior angle property, the exterior angle PRS equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles (angle QPR + angle PQR). Therefore, 110 degrees = angle QPR + 45 degrees, so angle QPR = 65 degrees.

questions.q: In a parallelogram ABCD, if angle A = (3x - 10) degrees and angle C = (2x + 30) degrees, find the value of x.
questions.explanation: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal. Therefore, angle A = angle C, so 3x - 10 = 2x + 30, giving x = 40.

faq.q: What is the angle sum of a quadrilateral?
faq.a: 360°. You can see this by splitting the quadrilateral into two triangles of 180° each.
For any simple polyhedron, Faces + Vertices − Edges = 2 (F + V − E = 2).
